records.source: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע־נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל־דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה׃
records.gloss: And but hear, please, Job, my speech, and all my words give ear [to].
pieces: But now, Job, please listen to what I say; \q pay attention to all my words.

L.1: But now, please hear my speech, Job, \q and give ear to all my words.

R.1: Now, Job, please listen to what I say. \q Pay attention to everything I tell you.

decisions.choice: Job: Elihu addresses Job by name
decisions.reason: Elihu turns from the friends (32:6-22) to Job himself, and calls him by name, as he does again in 33:31 and 37:14. The three friends never address Job by name in their speeches.

decisions.choice: but now: a turn to a new address
decisions.reason: The word ('ulam) marks a strong contrast or a new start: having explained himself to the friends, Elihu now speaks to Job.

decisions.choice: pay attention to (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Give ear" is the Hebrew picture of listening; Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable use the everyday phrase.

records.heading: Elihu speaks to Job

records.source: הִנֵּה־נָ֭א פָּתַ֣חְתִּי פִ֑י דִּבְּרָ֖ה לְשׁוֹנִ֣י בְחִכִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Look, please, I open my mouth; speaks my tongue in my palate.
pieces: Look, I have opened my mouth; \q my tongue is forming words in my mouth.

L.2: Look, now, I open my mouth; \q my tongue speaks in my palate.

R.2: I am ready to speak. \q The words are on the tip of my tongue.

decisions.choice: open my mouth, my tongue speaks in my palate: I am about to speak
decisions.reason: To open the mouth is to begin to speak (3:1). The palate or roof of the mouth is where words are shaped (6:30; Proverbs 8:7). Elihu announces at length, almost solemnly, that he is ready to begin.

decisions.choice: I am ready to speak; on the tip of my tongue (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean in common English idiom (m1).

records.source: יֹֽשֶׁר־לִבִּ֥י אֲמָרָ֑י וְדַ֥עַת שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י בָּר֥וּר מִלֵּֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] uprightness of my heart [are] my words, and [the] knowledge of my lips purely they utter.
pieces: My words come from an upright heart, \q and my lips speak what I know sincerely.

L.3: My words [are from the] uprightness of my heart, \q and what my lips know they utter purely.

R.3: I speak honestly, from my heart. \q I will tell you sincerely what I know.

decisions.choice: uprightness: honesty, straightness
decisions.reason: The word (yosher) comes from the same root as "upright" in 1:1. Elihu claims that his words come from an honest heart, with no hidden aim.

decisions.choice: purely: clearly, sincerely
decisions.reason: The word (barur) means clean, pure, picked out (Zephaniah 3:9, "pure lips"). What Elihu knows, he will say plainly and without mixture.

decisions.choice: I speak honestly, from my heart (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun phrase "the uprightness of my heart" into a short sentence.

records.source: רֽוּחַ־אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: [The] spirit of God has made me, and [the] breath of [the] Almighty gives me life.
pieces: The Spirit of God has made me; \q the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

L.4: The Spirit of God has made me, \q and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

R.4: God's Spirit made me. \q The breath of God All-Powerful gives me life.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God: God's own life-giving spirit, his breath
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) means wind, breath or spirit. Here it is God's own, and it stands beside "the breath of the Almighty": God made the first human from dust and breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7), and his spirit gives and sustains all life (Psalm 104:30; Job 27:3; 34:14-15). Elihu says that he, like Job, is God's creature (verse 6), and that his understanding comes from the same breath of God (32:8).

decisions.choice: the Almighty: Shaddai
decisions.reason: Shaddai, an ancient name of God, is rendered "the Almighty" (see 5:17).

decisions.choice: Spirit, with a capital S
decisions.reason: The spirit here belongs to God, as in "the Spirit of God" in Genesis 1:2, so it is capitalized, as the Spirit of the LORD is in Judges. In 32:8, where the spirit is spoken of as it is in a human being, it is lowercase. "Breath" is kept for the parallel word in the second line.

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "God All-Powerful" for Shaddai in every book.

records.source: אִם־תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה׃
records.gloss: If you are able, answer me; set in order before me; take your stand.
pieces: Answer me if you can; \q prepare your case before me \q and take your stand.

L.5: If you can, answer me; \q set [your case] in order before me; \q take your stand.

R.5: Answer me if you can. \q Get your arguments ready \q and stand up to me.

decisions.choice: set in order: arrange your case
decisions.reason: The verb ('arakh) is used for laying out a legal case (13:18; 23:4) and for drawing up a battle line. Job had said he would set out his case before God (23:4); Elihu invites him to set it out before him.

decisions.choice: take your stand: stand firm, as in court or battle
decisions.reason: The verb (yatsav in the reflexive) means to take up one's position and stand ready (1 Samuel 17:16; Psalm 2:2).

decisions.choice: your case (Literal, Balanced); your arguments (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object in Hebrew; the context of argument supplies it (m1).

records.source: הֵן־אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם־אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] like your mouth to God; from clay was pinched off also I.
pieces: Look, before God I am just as you are; \q I too was shaped from clay.

L.6: Look, I [am] as you [are] before God; \q I too was pinched off from clay.

R.6: You and I are the same in God's eyes. \q I too was made from clay.

decisions.choice: like your mouth to God: just as you are before God
alternatives: as you asked, I stand in God's place
decisions.reason: "Like your mouth" means "like you", "equal to you" (as "according to the mouth" can mean "in proportion to"). Elihu says he stands before God on the same footing as Job. The phrase can also mean "according to your word": Job had asked to argue with someone who would not overwhelm him (9:34-35; 13:21), and Elihu offers to be that one.

decisions.choice: pinched off from clay: shaped by God like a potter's work
decisions.reason: A potter nips off a piece of clay to shape a vessel. Humans are made from the ground (Genesis 2:7), and Job himself said God had shaped him like clay (10:9; see 4:19). The verb (qarats) is used for pinching or nipping.

decisions.choice: shaped (Balanced); made (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the potter's action; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2).

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֭מָתִי לֹ֣א תְבַעֲתֶ֑ךָּ וְ֝אַכְפִּ֗י עָלֶ֥יךָ לֹא־יִכְבָּֽד׃
records.gloss: Look, dread of me not will terrify you, and my pressure on you not will be heavy.
pieces: So no fear of me need terrify you, \q and my pressure will not weigh heavily on you.

L.7: Look, dread of me will not terrify you, \q and my pressure will not be heavy on you.

R.7: You do not need to be afraid of me. \q I will not be hard on you.

decisions.choice: dread of me will not terrify you: an echo of Job's words
decisions.reason: Job had asked God to take away his hand and not let dread of him terrify him, so that he could speak (9:34; 13:21). Elihu takes up the same words: as a fellow creature, he will not overwhelm Job.

decisions.choice: my pressure: my weight upon you
decisions.reason: The word ('ekhef) occurs only here; it seems to mean pressure or burden, from a root meaning to press. The ancient Greek translation reads "my hand", which fits Job's words in 13:21, "take your hand far from me".

decisions.choice: So (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Look" here draws a conclusion from verse 6; Balanced says "So", and Readable leaves the word out.

records.source: אַ֭ךְ אָמַ֣רְתָּ בְאָזְנָ֑י וְק֖וֹל מִלִּ֣ין אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
records.gloss: Surely you have spoken in my ears, and [the] sound of words I heard.
pieces: You have surely spoken in my hearing, \q and I have heard the sound of your words:

L.8: Surely you have spoken in my ears, \q and I heard the sound of [your] words:

R.8: I have heard what you said; \q I heard your words with my own ears:

decisions.choice: you have spoken: Elihu begins to sum up Job's words (verses 9-11)
decisions.reason: Elihu now quotes, in his own summary, what Job has claimed, before answering it in verse 12. Hebrew has no quotation marks; the colon at the end of the verse introduces the words.

decisions.choice: your words
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "words"; the context makes clear they are Job's, which Literal brackets.

records.source: זַ֥ךְ אֲנִ֗י בְּֽלִ֫י פָ֥שַׁע חַ֥ף אָנֹכִ֑י וְלֹ֖א עָוֺ֣ן לִֽי׃
records.gloss: Pure I [am], without transgression; clean I [am], and not iniquity [is] to me.
pieces: I am pure, without transgression; \q I am clean, \q and there is no guilt in me.

L.9: I [am] pure, without transgression; \q I [am] clean, \q and there [is] no iniquity in me.

R.9: I am pure and have done nothing wrong. \q I am clean; there is no sin in me.

decisions.choice: Elihu's summary of Job's claims, not an exact quotation
decisions.reason: Job had insisted on his innocence (9:21; 10:7; 16:17; 23:10-12; 27:5-6; chapter 31), but he never said that he was without any sin: he spoke of the sins of his youth (13:26) and asked why God did not pardon his wrongdoing (7:21). Elihu sharpens Job's words into a claim of complete purity.

decisions.choice: clean: washed clean
decisions.reason: The word (chaf) occurs only here; it is related to a verb for washing or rubbing clean. It stands beside "pure" (zakh, 8:6; 11:4).

decisions.choice: guilt (Balanced); sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word ('avon) means wrongdoing and the guilt it brings; Literal keeps the traditional "iniquity".

records.source: הֵ֣ן תְּ֭נוּאוֹת עָלַ֣י יִמְצָ֑א יַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Look, occasions against me he finds; he counts me as an enemy to him.
pieces: Yet God finds reasons to oppose me; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} counts me as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemy.

L.10: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} finds pretexts against me; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} counts me as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemy.

R.10: But God looks for reasons to attack me. \q He treats me as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemy.

decisions.choice: pretexts: occasions for hostility, excuses to oppose
decisions.reason: The word (tenu'ot) is rare; in Numbers 14:34 it means God's opposition or turning against Israel. Here it means grounds God seeks for treating Job as an opponent.

decisions.choice: counts me as his enemy: Job's own words
decisions.reason: Job asked God why he counted him as his enemy (13:24) and said that God counted him among his foes (19:11). Elihu quotes him almost word for word.

decisions.choice: God (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Job is speaking of God; Balanced and Readable name him the first time so that "he" is clear.

records.source: יָשֵׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֣ד רַגְלָ֑י יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כָּל־אָרְחֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: He puts in the stocks my feet; he watches all my paths.
pieces: He puts my feet in the stocks; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} watches all my paths.

L.11: He puts my feet in the stocks; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} watches all my paths.

R.11: He locks my feet in the stocks \q and watches every step I take.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Job's words in 13:27
decisions.reason: Job said: "You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths" (13:27). Elihu repeats the line, turned into the third person.

decisions.choice: the stocks: a wooden frame holding a prisoner's feet
decisions.reason: The stocks held a prisoner's feet fast so that he could not move (Jeremiah 20:2; Acts 16:24). Job pictures himself as God's prisoner, watched at every step.

decisions.choice: every step I take (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "paths" stands for: every step of Job's life.

records.source: הֶן־זֹ֣את לֹא־צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: Look, [in] this not you are right, I will answer you, for is greater God than a mortal.
pieces: But in this you are not right, I tell you, \q for God is greater than any human.

L.12: Look, [in] this you are not right, I will answer you, \q for God is greater than a mortal.

R.12: But I tell you, you are wrong about this, \q because God is greater than any human being.

decisions.choice: you are not right: you are not in the right in this
decisions.reason: The verb (tsadaq) is the court word Job used of himself (9:2; 13:18): to be in the right. Elihu does not say that Job is wicked, but that he is wrong in this charge against God.

decisions.choice: God is greater than a mortal: God is not to be judged by human measure
decisions.reason: Elihu's first answer is that God's greatness puts him beyond a human's charges. He goes on to say that God does speak to humans, though they may not notice (verses 13-30).

decisions.choice: But (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Look" here turns to Elihu's reply; Balanced and Readable say "But".

records.source: מַ֭דּוּעַ אֵלָ֣יו רִיב֑וֹתָ כִּ֥י כָל־דְּ֝בָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א־יַעֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Why against him have you contended, that all his words not he answers?
pieces: Why do you complain against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answers none of a person's words?

L.13: Why do you contend against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q [saying] that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not answer any of his words?

R.13: Why do you argue with God, \q saying that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never answers anyone?

decisions.choice: his words: a person's words, which God does not answer
alternatives: he gives no account of any of his own words or deeds
decisions.reason: "His" can refer to a human: Job complained that God would not answer him (19:7; 30:20; 31:35), and verses 14-30 reply that God does speak. Or it can refer to God: he gives no account of what he does. The first fits Elihu's answer better.

decisions.choice: contend: bring a case, quarrel
decisions.reason: The verb (riv) is used of a lawsuit (9:3; 10:2; 23:6). Job had wanted to take God to court.

decisions.choice: God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names God where the Hebrew has "him".

records.source: כִּֽי־בְאַחַ֥ת יְדַבֶּר־אֵ֑ל וּ֝בִשְׁתַּ֗יִם לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: For in one God speaks, and in two not one perceives it.
pieces: For God speaks in one way, and in another, \q though people do not notice it.

L.14: For God speaks in one [way], \q and in two, [yet one] does not perceive it.

R.14: God speaks again and again in different ways, \q but people do not notice.

decisions.choice: in one, and in two: more than once, in more than one way
decisions.reason: The pattern "one ... two" means repeatedly or in more than one way (40:5; Psalm 62:12). Elihu goes on to name two ways God speaks: dreams (verses 15-18) and suffering (verses 19-28).

decisions.choice: one does not perceive it: people fail to notice
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means people in general. God speaks, but people do not take it in.

records.source: בַּחֲל֤וֹם׀חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֣ל תַּ֭רְדֵּמָה עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֑ים בִּ֝תְנוּמ֗וֹת עֲלֵ֣י מִשְׁכָּֽב׃
records.gloss: In a dream, a vision of [the] night, when falls deep sleep on men, in slumbers on [the] bed,
pieces: In a dream, a vision in the night, \q when deep sleep falls on people \q as they slumber on their beds,

L.15: In a dream, a vision of [the] night, \q when deep sleep falls on people, \q in slumbers on [the] bed,

R.15: God speaks in dreams and visions at night, \q when people are sound asleep in their beds.

decisions.choice: a vision of the night, deep sleep: words Eliphaz used
decisions.reason: Eliphaz described his night vision with the same words: "in visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people" (4:13). Job too spoke of frightening dreams and visions (7:14).

decisions.choice: deep sleep: heavy, unnatural sleep
decisions.reason: The word (tardemah) is the deep sleep God brought on Adam (Genesis 2:21) and on Abraham (Genesis 15:12).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 16
decisions.reason: Verse 15 sets the scene; verse 16 says what God does then.

decisions.choice: God speaks (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes verse 15 a sentence of its own, supplying the subject and verb from verse 14.

records.source: אָ֣ז יִ֭גְלֶה אֹ֣זֶן אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּבְמֹ֖סָרָ֣ם יַחְתֹּֽם׃
records.gloss: Then he uncovers [the] ear of men, and with their discipline he seals.
pieces: then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opens people's ears \q and seals {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} warning upon them,

L.16: then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} uncovers the ear of people, \q and seals [them] with their instruction,

R.16: God opens their ears \q and seals {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} warning in their minds.

decisions.choice: uncover the ear: reveal something to someone
decisions.reason: To uncover someone's ear is to tell them something, often a secret (1 Samuel 9:15; 20:2; 2 Samuel 7:27). Elihu uses the phrase again in 36:10, 15.

decisions.choice: seals their instruction: stamps the warning firmly on them
decisions.reason: The word (musar) is discipline or instruction that corrects. To seal it is to make it firm and lasting, as a seal marks a document. The ancient Greek translation read a similar-looking verb, "he terrifies them" with visions, as in 7:14.

decisions.choice: his warning (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The instruction is God's, given to them; Balanced and Readable say "his warning", which is what the correction is in verses 17-18.

records.source: לְ֭הָסִיר אָדָ֣ם מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְגֵוָ֖ה מִגֶּ֣בֶר יְכַסֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: To turn aside a human [from his] deed, and pride from a man he covers.
pieces: to turn people away from what they are doing \q and keep them from pride.

L.17: to turn a human aside [from his] deed, \q and to cover pride from a man.

R.17: He does this to turn people away from doing wrong \q and to keep them from becoming proud.

decisions.choice: to turn aside: the purpose of God's warnings
decisions.reason: Verses 17-18 say why God speaks in the night: to turn a person away from a wrong course before it is too late. The warning is an act of mercy.

decisions.choice: deed: here a wrong course of action
decisions.reason: The word (ma'aseh) simply means a deed or work; the context shows it is a deed that leads to death (verse 18).

decisions.choice: cover pride from a man: put pride out of his reach, hide it from him
decisions.reason: The verb (kasah) means to cover or hide. God conceals pride from the person, keeping him from it. Some suggest the verb should be read with a similar one meaning "cut off"; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: generic person: Literal keeps the singular "he"; Balanced and Readable say "they"
decisions.reason: Elihu describes any human being whom God warns (verse 14), using masculine singular words as Hebrew does for anyone. Literal keeps the singular; Balanced and Readable use "people" and "they" through verses 17-30, which also keeps the person apart from God, who is "he".

records.source: יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ מֵעֲבֹ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁלַח׃
records.gloss: He keeps back his soul from [the] pit, and his life from passing over by [the] weapon.
pieces: He spares them from the pit, \q their life from perishing by the sword.

L.18: He keeps back his soul from [the] pit, \q and his life from passing over by [the] weapon.

R.18: He saves them from the grave \q and keeps them from dying a violent death.

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave, the world of the dead
decisions.reason: The word (shachat) means a pit and, as in verses 22, 24, 28 and 30, the grave and the realm of death (17:14; Psalm 16:10). Elihu returns to it five times in this chapter.

decisions.choice: passing over by the weapon: perishing by a violent death
decisions.reason: The word (shelach) usually means a weapon, a spear or missile (2 Chronicles 23:10; Joel 2:8). Some take it here as a channel or river, the stream to be crossed into the world of the dead, which would fit the parallel "pit". Either way the line speaks of death.

decisions.choice: his soul: his life, himself
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) means the living self, the person; it stands beside "his life" in the second line.

decisions.choice: them, their life (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for "his soul" (m3) and keep the generic plural (verse 17).

records.source: וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל־מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ וְר֖וֹב עֲצָמָ֣יו אֵתָֽן׃
records.gloss: And he is rebuked with pain on his bed, and [the] multitude of his bones [is] constant.
pieces: People are also corrected by pain on their beds, \q with constant aching in all their bones.

L.19: And he is rebuked with pain on his bed, \q and the multitude of his bones [with] constant [pain].

R.19: Or God may correct people by making them sick in bed, \q with constant pain in every bone.

decisions.choice: and he is rebuked: the second way God speaks
decisions.reason: Having described warnings in dreams (verses 15-18), Elihu turns to the second way God speaks: through illness and pain (verses 19-28).

decisions.choice: rebuked: corrected, disciplined
decisions.reason: The verb (yakach) is the one Elihu used for refuting in 32:12. Here God corrects a person through suffering, as in 5:17 and Proverbs 3:11-12.

decisions.choice: the multitude of his bones (read), not "strife in his bones" (written)
alternatives: and the strife in his bones is constant
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) give "strife" (riv): "constant strife in his bones". The scribes marked the word to be read as "multitude" (rov): all his many bones are in constant pain. The word data follows the reading, and so does this translation. The sense is much the same: the pain fills the whole body without rest.

decisions.choice: constant [pain]
decisions.reason: The line has no word for pain; it is understood from the first line. Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: God may correct (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the passive into an active sentence and names God as the one who corrects (m2).

records.source: וְזִֽהֲמַ֣תּוּ חַיָּת֣וֹ לָ֑חֶם וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מַאֲכַ֥ל תַּאֲוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And makes loathsome it his life, bread, and his soul food of desire.
pieces: They come to loathe food, \q even the food they most enjoy.

L.20: And his life loathes bread, \q and his soul desirable food.

R.20: They lose their appetite \q and cannot stand even their favorite food.

decisions.choice: his life, his soul: he himself, as one who hungers
decisions.reason: Both words (chayyah and nefesh) mean the living self; nefesh is often the seat of appetite (Psalm 107:18, "their soul loathed all food"). The sick man has no desire to eat.

decisions.choice: loathes: finds it disgusting
decisions.reason: The verb (zaham) is found only here; it means to make or find something loathsome.

decisions.choice: food; the food they most enjoy (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general; Balanced and Readable say "food".

records.source: יִ֣כֶל בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מֵרֹ֑אִי וְשֻׁפּ֥וּ עַ֝צְמוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א רֻאּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Wastes away his flesh from sight, and are laid bare his bones [which] not were seen.
pieces: Their flesh wastes away until it can hardly be seen, \q and their bones, once hidden, stick out.

L.21: His flesh wastes away from sight, \q and his bones, [which] were not seen, are laid bare.

R.21: They get so thin that their flesh almost disappears, \q and bones that were once hidden now stick out.

decisions.choice: wastes away from sight: grows so thin it is no longer seen
decisions.reason: The flesh shrinks until little of it is left to see, while the bones, once covered, show through the skin (19:20; Psalm 102:6).

decisions.choice: are laid bare (read)
decisions.reason: The written consonants and the reading the scribes marked differ by one letter; the reading, which the word data follows, gives "are laid bare". The sense is the same.

records.source: וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים׃
records.gloss: And draws near to the pit his soul, and his life to those who bring death.
pieces: They draw near to the pit, \q their life to those who bring death.

L.22: And his soul draws near to the pit, \q and his life to those who bring death.

R.22: They come close to the grave, \q close to those who bring death.

decisions.choice: those who bring death: the destroyers, perhaps angels of death
decisions.reason: The word is a participle, "those who cause death". It may mean destroying angels such as the one sent against Jerusalem (2 Samuel 24:16) or the destroyer of Exodus 12:23; they stand in contrast to the angel who rescues in verse 23. By a small change in the vowels some read "to the dead".

decisions.choice: they, their life (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, "his soul" is the person himself; Balanced and Readable keep the generic plural.

records.source: אִם־יֵ֤שׁ עָלָ֨יו׀מַלְאָ֗ךְ מֵלִ֗יץ אֶחָ֥ד מִנִּי־אָ֑לֶף לְהַגִּ֖יד לְאָדָ֣ם יָשְׁרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: If there is for him an angel, a mediator, one from a thousand, to declare to a human his uprightness,
pieces: If there is an angel beside them, \q a mediator, one out of a thousand, \q to tell them what is right for them,

L.23: If there is an angel for him, \q a mediator, one out of a thousand, \q to declare to a human his uprightness,

R.23: But an angel may be there to help them, \q a go-between, one out of a thousand, \q to show them the right way to live.

decisions.choice: an angel: a heavenly messenger
decisions.reason: The word (mal'akh) means a messenger, human or heavenly. Set against "those who bring death" (verse 22) and pleading for a ransom (verse 24), this one is most likely a heavenly being. Eliphaz had asked to which of the holy ones Job would turn (5:1).

decisions.choice: a mediator: one who speaks between two parties
decisions.reason: The word (melits) is used of an interpreter (Genesis 42:23) and of envoys (2 Chronicles 32:31). Here it is one who speaks for a person before God. Job had longed for an arbiter between himself and God (9:33) and a witness in heaven (16:19-21). "One out of a thousand" means a rare one, one among many angels.

decisions.choice: his uprightness: what is right for him to do
decisions.reason: "His uprightness" most likely means the upright way the person should take: the angel shows him his duty, so that he turns back to God. Some take it as the person's uprightness, which the angel vouches for, or as God's uprightness.

decisions.choice: generic person: Literal keeps the singular "he"; Balanced and Readable say "they"
decisions.reason: Elihu describes any human being whom God warns (verse 14), using masculine singular words as Hebrew does for anyone. Literal keeps the singular; Balanced and Readable use "people" and "they" through verses 17-30, which also keeps the person apart from God, who is "he".

decisions.choice: But an angel may be there; a go-between (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the condition into a statement of what may happen, and uses a plain word for mediator.

records.source: וַיְחֻנֶּ֗נּוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּ֭דָעֵהוּ מֵרֶ֥דֶת שָׁ֗חַת מָצָ֥אתִי כֹֽפֶר׃
records.gloss: And he is gracious to him and says, Deliver him from going down [to the] pit; I have found a ransom.
pieces: and he is gracious to them and says, \q Spare them from going down to the pit; \q I have found a ransom.

L.24: and he is gracious to him and says, \q Deliver him from going down to [the] pit; \q I have found a ransom.

R.24: and he shows them mercy and says, \q Save them from going down to the grave; \q I have found a ransom.

decisions.choice: he: God, or the angel
decisions.reason: The verse does not name who is gracious and who speaks. Most likely it is God, who accepts the angel's plea and orders the person spared; it may be the angel, who appeals to God with the words "deliver him". Since the text leaves it open, no level names him.

decisions.choice: a ransom: a price paid to free a life
decisions.reason: The word (kofer) is the payment that releases a life otherwise forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12; Psalm 49:8). Elihu does not say what the ransom is; it may be the person's repentance (verse 27) or the angel's plea itself.

decisions.choice: deliver: rescue
decisions.reason: This verb form occurs only here. It is usually taken as a form of the verb "to redeem, ransom" (padah), which comes in verse 28, or as a word meaning "to deliver".

records.source: רֻֽטֲפַ֣שׁ בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מִנֹּ֑עַר יָ֝שׁ֗וּב לִימֵ֥י עֲלוּמָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Grows fresh his flesh more than youth; he returns to [the] days of his youthful vigor.
pieces: Their flesh becomes fresher than a child's; \q they return to the days of their youthful strength.

L.25: His flesh grows fresher than [in] youth; \q he returns to the days of his youthful vigor.

R.25: Their body becomes as fresh as a child's, \q and they are as strong as they were when they were young.

decisions.choice: grows fresh: becomes full and healthy again
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here; from the context it means to grow fresh, soft or plump, the opposite of the wasting in verse 21.

decisions.choice: fresher than youth: like the healing of Naaman
decisions.reason: When Naaman was healed, "his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child" (2 Kings 5:14). The word for youth here (na'ar) can mean a young boy or child.

records.source: יֶעְתַּ֤ר אֶל־אֱל֨וֹהַּ׀וַיִּרְצֵ֗הוּ וַיַּ֣רְא פָּ֭נָיו בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׁב לֶ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ צִדְקָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He prays to God and he accepts him, and he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to a mortal his righteousness.
pieces: They pray to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accepts them; \q they see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face with shouts of joy, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} restores them to righteousness.

L.26: He prays to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accepts him; \q and he sees {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face with a shout of joy, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} restores to [the] mortal his righteousness.

R.26: They pray to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is pleased with them. \q They come into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence and shout for joy, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives them back their right standing.

decisions.choice: accepts: is pleased with, receives with favor
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsah) is used of God accepting a person or an offering with pleasure (Genesis 33:10; Psalm 147:11). The prayer is heard.

decisions.choice: sees his face: comes before God in worship
decisions.reason: To see God's face is to come into his presence, especially in worship at the sanctuary (Psalm 17:15; 42:3). The restored person sees God's face, not with dread but with shouts of joy, the cry raised at festivals (Psalm 27:6; 89:16).

decisions.choice: restores his righteousness: gives back his right standing with God
alternatives: he declares to people God's righteousness
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring back or restore. God treats the person as righteous again, accepted and in the right. Some take the person as the subject: he tells others of God's righteousness, leading into his song in verse 27.

decisions.choice: generic person: Literal keeps the singular "he"; Balanced and Readable say "they"
decisions.reason: Elihu describes any human being whom God warns (verse 14), using masculine singular words as Hebrew does for anyone. Literal keeps the singular; Balanced and Readable use "people" and "they" through verses 17-30, which also keeps the person apart from God, who is "he".

records.source: יָשֹׁ֤ר׀עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָ֭טָאתִי וְיָשָׁ֥ר הֶעֱוֵ֗יתִי וְלֹא־שָׁ֥וָה לִֽי׃
records.gloss: He sings before men and says, I have sinned and [the] right I have perverted, and not it was repaid to me.
pieces: Then they sing before others and say, \q I sinned and twisted what was right, \q but I was not repaid as I deserved.

L.27: He sings before people and says, \q I sinned and perverted what was right, \q and it was not repaid to me.

R.27: Then they sing in front of everyone and say, \q I sinned and did what was wrong, \q but God did not punish me as I deserved.

decisions.choice: sings: sings out before others
decisions.reason: The verb can come from a root meaning "to sing" (shir) or one meaning "to look" (shur). The rescued person's public confession and thanks (as in Psalm 22:23-26; 40:10-11) suits "sings"; the word data's gloss takes it as "looks".

decisions.choice: it was not repaid to me: I was not punished as I deserved
alternatives: it was not worth it to me
decisions.reason: The verb (shavah) means to be equal or match. The person admits that the suffering did not match the sin: God spared him what he deserved. Some take it to mean that the sin did not profit him.

decisions.choice: and says: the song is a confession
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no quotation marks; the person's words begin after "says" and, in the written text, run through verse 28 (see 28 m1).

decisions.choice: God did not punish me (Readable)
alternatives: it was not repaid to me
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who held back the punishment (m2).

records.source: פָּדָ֣ה נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מֵעֲבֹ֣ר בַּשָּׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּתוֹ בָּא֥וֹר תִּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: He has redeemed his soul from passing into the pit, and his life on the light will look.
pieces: God has redeemed them from going down to the pit, \q and they will live to see the light.

L.28: He has redeemed his soul from passing into the pit, \q and his life will look on the light.

R.28: God has saved them from going down to the grave, \q and they will live and enjoy the light.

decisions.choice: his soul, his life (read), not "my soul, my life" (written)
alternatives: He has redeemed my soul from passing into the pit, and my life will look on the light
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) say "my soul ... my life", so the verse continues the rescued person's song: "He redeemed my soul ... and my life will see the light." The scribes marked the words to be read as "his soul ... his life", so that Elihu speaks again about the person. The word data follows the reading, and so does this translation. The meaning is the same: God has rescued the person from death.

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free by paying a price
decisions.reason: The verb (padah) is the one used for buying back a life (Exodus 13:13; Psalm 49:16). It answers the ransom of verse 24.

decisions.choice: look on the light: live
decisions.reason: To see the light is to be alive (3:16, 20; Psalm 49:20). The person who was near the pit (verse 22) will go on living.

decisions.choice: God (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who redeems, since "he" could be taken for the angel or the person.

records.source: הֶן־כָּל־אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל־אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם־גָּֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: Look, all these God does, twice, three times, with a man,
pieces: Look, God does all these things \q two or three times with a person,

L.29: Look, all these [things] God does \q twice, three times with a man,

R.29: God does all these things for people \q again and again,

decisions.choice: twice, three times: again and again
decisions.reason: The pairing of numbers means repeatedly (as "one ... two" in verse 14). God's patience gives a person more than one chance.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 30
decisions.reason: Verse 30 gives the purpose of all God's ways of speaking.

decisions.choice: generic person: Literal keeps the singular "he"; Balanced and Readable say "they"
decisions.reason: Elihu describes any human being whom God warns (verse 14), using masculine singular words as Hebrew does for anyone. Literal keeps the singular; Balanced and Readable use "people" and "they" through verses 17-30, which also keeps the person apart from God, who is "he".

records.source: לְהָשִׁ֣יב נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת לֵ֝א֗וֹר בְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַיִּים׃
records.gloss: To bring back his soul from [the] pit, to be lit with the light of life.
pieces: to bring them back from the pit, \q so that the light of life may shine on them.

L.30: to bring back his soul from [the] pit, \q to be lit up with the light of life.

R.30: to bring them back from the grave \q so that they can enjoy the light of life.

decisions.choice: the light of life: life itself
decisions.reason: The phrase means being alive in the world of the living, as against the darkness of the grave (Psalm 56:14). It sums up verses 28-30.

decisions.choice: to bring back, to be lit up: the purpose of God's dealings
decisions.reason: The two infinitives say why God does all this (verse 29): not to destroy but to bring the person back to life.

decisions.choice: them (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, "his soul" is the person; Balanced and Readable say "them".

records.source: הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: Pay attention, Job; listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
pieces: Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; \q be quiet, and I will speak.

L.31: Pay attention, Job; listen to me; \q be silent, and I will speak.

R.31: Job, pay attention and listen to me. \q Be quiet and let me speak.

decisions.choice: Elihu calls Job by name again and asks for silence
decisions.reason: Elihu ends this speech as he began it (verse 1). He asks Job both to answer (verse 32) and to be silent (verses 31, 33); Job never answers Elihu.

records.source: אִם־יֵשׁ־מִלִּ֥ין הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי דַּ֝בֵּ֗ר כִּֽי־חָפַ֥צְתִּי צַדְּקֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: If there are words, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.
pieces: If you have anything to say, answer me; \q speak, for I want to see you proved right.

L.32: If there are words, answer me; \q speak, for I desire to justify you.

R.32: If you have something to say, answer me. \q Speak, because I would like to see you proved right.

decisions.choice: justify you: show you to be in the right
decisions.reason: The verb (tsadaq in the intensive) means to declare or show someone to be in the right. Elihu was angry because Job justified himself (32:2); now he says that he would gladly see Job in the right, if Job can make his case.

decisions.choice: anything to say (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "If there are words" means if Job has a reply; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: אִם־אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: If not, you listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
pieces: If not, then listen to me; \q be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.

L.33: If not, you listen to me; \q be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

R.33: If not, then listen to me. \q Be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.

decisions.choice: if not: if you have nothing to say
decisions.reason: "If not" answers "if there are words" in verse 32. The "you" is emphatic: then you, for your part, listen. Elihu's next speech begins in chapter 34.
